facts.statement: The first fossils of Gasparinisaura were discovered in 1992 near Cinco Saltos in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Gasparinisaura were found in 1992 near Cinco Saltos in Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus name Gasparinisaura honors the Argentine paleontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini.
facts.quote: The generic name honors Argentine palaeontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MUCPv-208 was uncovered in 1992 from the Anacleto Formation, dating to about 83 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, MUCPv-208, was uncovered in 1992 in a layer of the Anacleto Formation, dating from the early Campanian, about 83 million years old.

facts.statement: Three additional specimens were described in 1997, representing juvenile individuals.
facts.quote: In 1997, three additional specimens were described: MUCPv 213, a partial skeleton with skull; MCSPv 111, a postcranial skeleton; and MCSPv 112, a skull with hindlimbs and pelvis.

facts.statement: Gastroliths associated with three juvenile specimens were described in 2008.
facts.quote: In 2008, gastroliths present with all three juvenile specimens were described.

facts.statement: Gasparinisaura was a small, bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Gasparinisaura was a small bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Gasparinisaura at 1.7 meters and its weight at 13 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 1.7 m and the weight at 13 kg.

facts.statement: Gasparinisaura possessed unique, low, plate-like triangular chevrons on its tail that expanded toward the back, a trait found only in Euornithopoda.
facts.quote: The tail featured low plate-like triangular chevrons that were expanded towards the back, which is unique in the Euornithopoda.

facts.statement: The gastroliths represented about 0.3% of the animal's total body weight, a mass considered sufficient to function as a gastric mill, unlike in sauropods where such stones are often too light.
facts.quote: Representing about 0.3% of total body weight, they were voluminous enough to function as a gastric mill, a function sometimes denied for sauropod gastroliths because of their insufficient relative mass, being an order of magnitude lower.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Gasparinisaura within the clade Elasmaria, a group of hypsilophodonts known from South America, Antarctica, and possibly Australia.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis included in the description of the Antarctic ornithopod Morrosaurus shows that the latter and Gasparinisaura are part of Elasmaria, a clade of hypsilophodonts known from South America, Antarctica and maybe Australia.

facts.statement: Gasparinisaura was a herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Gasparinisaura (meaning "Gasparini's lizard") is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The species name cincosaltensis refers to the location Cinco Saltos.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to Cinco Saltos.

facts.statement: Originally, the describers considered Gasparinisaura to be a very basal iguanodontian and the most primitive member of the clade Euiguanodontia.
facts.quote: Originalmente fue considerado por sus descriptores como un iguanodontiano muy basal, el miembro más primitivo del clado Euiguanodontia.

facts.statement: Gasparinisaura could be the most basal member of the Elasmaria group.
facts.quote: Gasparinisaura podría ser el miembro más basal de este grupo.

facts.statement: In 2026, Dieudonné, Paulina-Carabajal, and Cruzado-Caballero redescribed the skull anatomy of Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis and named a new clade, Dysalotosaurinae, within Dryosauridae.
facts.quote: Dieudonné, Paulina-Carabajal & Cruzado-Caballero (2026) redescribe the anatomy of the skull of Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis, and name a new clade Dysalotosaurinae within Dryosauridae.
